account:
Today I attended morning office business and went to the mill for the ten-o'clock grain inspection. The appointment book did not identify a host, and we have not found the mill's responsible keeper. I saw 128 hay bales for sale at two emeralds each—1,152 wheat equivalent—but did not establish storage or delivery conditions. I asked the secretary to find the keeper through the baker and arrange a follow-up.

The unusual matter is repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' discussed at the bakery. Townsfolk named the baker and freight, and one report also named the neighbour. I have not heard the actual discussion or seen a proposal establishing what change is intended. Repetition may simply be the same rumour spreading. Reports of the baker carrying bread and wheat seem consistent with ordinary bakery business; they do not establish wrongdoing. I asked the secretary to clarify the discussion directly. A freight proposal was among the office papers I returned earlier, but I do not presently have its contents to connect it confidently with this talk.

The builder has just reported a visual inspection of the bridge and public lanterns along several routes, finding no specific defects. He explicitly did not claim a complete structural survey or nighttime lighting test. He made no repairs or purchases and proposed no charges. I requested written findings for the secretary and maintained the requirement for authorization before spending.

My tentative thought is that the bakery conversation may concern transport, deliveries, or proposed public works, but I do not know its purpose. Nothing I have personally established shows a secret scheme or an authorized change. I want firsthand explanations from those involved, rather than accusations based on rumour. I am now slightly late returning from lunch for one-o'clock council letters; tea with the neighbour at three may also offer an opportunity to ask what was discussed.
